title: Lesson 3: Nikhilam — Multiply Near Any Base (10, 100, 1000)
learningGoals: Apply the Nikhilam sutra to multiply numbers near 10, 100, and 1000 without long multiplication.
Choose the most efficient base for any given multiplication problem.
Extend Nikhilam to sub-bases like 50 and 500 for versatile mental arithmetic.
coreIdeas: Nikhilam Navatascharamam Dashatah: All from 9, last from 10 — but here used for base multiplication.
Write each number's excess/deficit from the chosen base. Cross-add for left part; multiply deviations for right part.
Right part must have as many digits as there are zeros in the base (1 digit for base 10, 2 for 100, 3 for 1000).

workedExamples.question: 9 × 8 (base 10)
workedExamples.method: Deviations: −1 and −2. Cross: 9−2=7. Right: 1×2=02 (1 digit). Answer: 72.

workedExamples.question: 98 × 97 (base 100)
workedExamples.method: Deviations: −2 and −3. Cross: 98−3=95. Right: 2×3=06 (2 digits). Answer: 9506.

workedExamples.question: 997 × 996 (base 1000)
workedExamples.method: Deviations: −3 and −4. Cross: 997−4=993. Right: 3×4=012 (3 digits). Answer: 993012.

starterPractice: Warm-up: What is the deviation of 97 from base 100?
Guided: Use Nikhilam near base 100 to find 98 × 96.

onboarding.coachIntro: Hello! I am Arya. Today we unlock the FULL power of Nikhilam — multiplying numbers near 10, 100, and 1000. You will be doing 3-digit multiplication in your head that would stun your classmates!
onboarding.placementRule: If the student correctly does Nikhilam near 10 in Group A, jump to Group B (near 100).

mission.missionPromise: Master 2-digit and 3-digit multiplication using bases 10, 100, and 1000. No long multiplication needed!
mission.successCelebration: Incredible! You multiplied 3-digit numbers near 1000 in your head. That is Vedic superpower!

microLessonPattern: Arya states the base and writes deviations visually in a table.
Student writes the deviation before attempting the multiplication.
Left part and right part are computed separately.
Right part is padded to the correct number of digits.
Instant feedback identifies which part (left or right) was incorrect.
